summary:
IGNIS (FIREINTEL) is an intelligent space-fire knowledge system developed to organize, analyze, and synthesize microgravity combustion research for deep-space exploration safety. It directly addresses NASA’s “Flame in Freefall” challenge by tackling the counter-intuitive physics of zero-gravity fires, where flames lose upward thermal buoyancy, form quiet spherical pockets, and propagate strictly along cabin ventilation currents.

To resolve the issue of scattered spaceflight research archives, we built a centralized dashboard featuring an interactive Combustion Propagation Matrix, standardized Experiment DNA profiling, a relational Knowledge Graph, an Artemis Research Gap Map, and a RAG-powered NASA AI Synthesis Agent.

This platform is vital for future space exploration because partial-gravity environments on the Moon (0.16g) and Mars (0.38g), operating under elevated oxygen atmospheres, remain major unmapped safety risks. IGNIS transforms static PDF reports into actionable telemetry intelligence, helping mission planners evaluate material flammability limits to safeguard crewed habitats.

IGNIS: FIREINTELL — Detailed Project Description

1. What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

IGNIS: FIREINTELL is an integrated, research-focused web dashboard designed to organize, explore, and interpret NASA's microgravity fire-safety research. Fires behave differently in microgravity than they do on Earth, making it essential to understand combustion processes to protect astronauts and future space habitats. However, relevant scientific information is distributed across multiple NASA databases, investigations, and technical publications.

IGNIS addresses this challenge by bringing together research information from four NASA sources: Physical Sciences Investigations (PSI), NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), NASA TechPort, and NASA Open Data.

The system follows a structured data pipeline:

  • Data Collection: Retrieves research information from NASA investigation pages, APIs, technical publications, and open datasets.
  • Data Preprocessing: Cleans, organizes, standardizes, and structures collected information to improve consistency and usability.
  • Database Management: Stores structured research records in a centralized PostgreSQL database.
  • Multimodal Search: Supports research discovery across available information formats and content types, helping users locate relevant scientific information through the dashboard.
  • Research Exploration: Allows users to explore investigations, technical publications, research projects, and experimental information through an interactive web interface.
  • Data Visualization: Presents research information through interactive charts, visual summaries, and searchable records, helping users understand and explore the collected data.
  • Source Traceability: Maintains source references so users can trace research information back to its original NASA investigation, publication, or dataset.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

IGNIS: FIREINTELL provides several benefits:

  • Centralized Research Access: Brings information from multiple NASA research sources into one platform.
  • Time Efficiency: Reduces the effort required to search through numerous individual research documents and databases.
  • Improved Research Understanding: Organizes experimental conditions, investigations, and publications into a more accessible format.
  • Enhanced Research Discovery: Multimodal search capabilities help users explore available scientific information more efficiently.
  • Data Transparency: Preserves source references to help users verify information.
  • Research Accessibility: Makes complex scientific information easier to explore for students, researchers, and space-science enthusiasts.
  • Knowledge Discovery: Helps users explore connections between different investigations, scientific publications, and research projects.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

The ultimate goal of IGNIS: FIREINTELL is to support safer human space exploration through better access to scientific knowledge.

Understanding combustion in microgravity is essential because flames behave differently in reduced-gravity environments. Research into flame behavior, ignition, extinction, and experimental conditions can contribute to improved fire-safety strategies for spacecraft and future space habitats.

By making existing NASA research easier to discover, organize, and interpret, IGNIS aims to support researchers, engineers, students, and future scientists working toward safer environments for astronauts.

Its potential impact extends to the development of safer space stations, lunar habitats, Mars missions, and other future human space-exploration environments.

4. What Tools, Programming Languages, and Software Were Used?

Our development process combines data engineering, database management, web technologies, search capabilities, and data visualization.

  • Python: Used for data collection, API integration, data extraction, cleaning, preprocessing, and dataset generation.
  • PostgreSQL: Used to design and maintain a structured relational database for storing and managing research information.
  • Multimodal Search: Used as a research discovery capability to help users explore available scientific information across supported content types.
  • HTML: Used to structure the web dashboard and its content.
  • CSS: Used to style the interface and create a consistent visual experience.
  • JavaScript: Used to implement interactive frontend functionality and dashboard components.
  • NASA APIs and Open Data Sources: Used to retrieve scientific investigations, technical publications, research projects, and relevant datasets.
  • Data Visualization: Used to transform structured research information into interactive and understandable visual representations.
  • Vercel: Used to deploy and host the web dashboard.
  • Visual Studio Code: Used as the primary development environment.

The project is software-based and does not require specialized physical hardware.

5. How Is the Project Creative and Innovative?

The creativity of IGNIS: FIREINTELL lies in transforming fragmented scientific information into a unified research exploration experience.

Rather than developing another static information website, our team focused on building a platform that connects different NASA research resources through a structured data pipeline, searchable research collections, and interactive visualizations.

Its innovative aspects include:

  • Integrating multiple NASA research sources into a unified research environment.
  • Combining data engineering, database management, and visualization to simplify scientific exploration.
  • Incorporating multimodal search capabilities to improve research discovery across supported content types.
  • Connecting investigations, publications, and research projects through organized information.
  • Emphasizing source traceability and research transparency.
  • Presenting complex microgravity combustion research in a format that is more approachable and useful to different audiences.

The project focuses not only on collecting scientific information but also on improving how people discover, navigate, and understand it.

6. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

During development, our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Relevance: Prioritizing research related to microgravity combustion and fire safety in space.
  • Data Reliability: Maintaining original source references and avoiding unsupported scientific conclusions.
  • Data Quality: Handling missing values, inconsistent formats, duplicate records, and incomplete metadata.
  • Scalability: Designing the data pipeline and database to accommodate additional NASA research sources and future datasets.
